procedure: This packet is source-only and executes nothing now. After independent review, dispatch SEVEN SEPARATE future selector controllers in listed order, one heavy body at a time. Placement9168 is excluded permanently from this packet.

Use the existing owner/tool session. The owner records the command and returned tool session ID in its normal controller log immediately. A tool yield, exec timeout, missing response, missing PID, missing lock, or missing normal artifact is never evidence of process death and never permission for another invocation.

Before the first invocation, authenticate the unchanged builder SHA/blob and all four exact detached clean checkouts, their SHA/tree pairs and existing request-checkout receipts/worker target metadata by read-only inspection. Native submit retains its own validation. No pins, queue, registry, kit, product or historical artifact edits by the controller.

Read native request files for BOTH exact preflight/normal suites, all potentially torn ID directories, exact registry rows, native artifact and existing .lock. Use inspection argv below. The inspector parses assignments as data; snap.key authenticates native command+App tree+suite+files+ext. All twelve cross-product pins are in the genuine command bytes. Any wrong source OR command OR row OR inconsistent hash, duplicate ID/row, mismatched artifact, missing native snap or unreadable custody is finite NOTRUN for THAT selector, not an ignored candidate. Preserve the first error and observed IDs.

ADOPT: use the exact existing normal ID whether queued, running, pass, fail, timeout, error or cancelled. Retain original request/snap/status/exit/summary and immutable checkout receipts in place. Do not rewrite the submit artifact, infer a body verdict from a request state, create another request, or invoke native submit. A request before normal-artifact persistence is adoptable only with authentic native row/request/snap-key binding. If native custody cannot supply this binding, return NOTRUN; no fabricated command receipt.

WAIT_EXISTING_TOOL_SESSION: resume/poll ONLY the originally returned exec session/cell (write_stdin for exec_command session_id, functions.wait only for its returned cell_id). Use <=60s poll intervals, retain session ownership, and repeat read-only inspection as native preflight/normal artifacts appear. Never call exec_command with the native argv a second time, never repeat printed request-test lines, and never substitute a PID observed through another sandbox for the retained tool session.

An existing preflight-only artifact/request with an ended or unknown owner cannot safely resume via unchanged native submit. Return finite NOTRUN for this selector even if the preflight passed or a lock appears stale. Do not reconstruct artifact IDs or alter/remove the native lock. A live owner may continue only its already-running invocation. This removes the former create_preflight/create_normal model path entirely.

FIRST_NATIVE_INVOCATION_ONLY: this is conditional on proven not-started ownership and an empty namespace (no request, artifact, lock or registered row). Repeat the same inspection immediately before exec. The existing sole owner is the only producer; no second controller of this selector may be launched between inspection and exec or during preflight/normal persistence. If another request appears after an earlier empty check, authenticate/adopt it or return NOTRUN; never proceed from the stale empty check. No new lease/guard/authorization is introduced. The native artifact file lock remains responsible for its own acquisition/release.

Measure ordinary admission once at dispatch: free bytes strictly above5200000000, one heavy at a time, no held routes. Start the genuine argv exactly once, cwd and explicit env below; remove conflicting inherited override keys listed below. Retain stdout/stderr and tool session in the existing owner record. Native --submit alone owns request-checkout, exact receipt validation, source preflight, row registration, preflight request+wait, normal request and artifact persistence. This packet never calls request-test directly.

After the original native tool session returns, wait/reap that same session, inspect again and authenticate the exact normal ID before observing its terminal. Existing native wait-test may observe ONLY that authenticated normal ID; exit124 means observe that SAME ID again, never resubmit. Retain actual native resultDir/d66, request/snap/status/exit/summary/log/trace in place. Submission output_path is private per selector; the service body independently sets D66_OUTPUT_DIR=resultDir/d66. No future IDs are invented in this packet.

The future controller owns a genuine 5s trace from its first tool and KEEP before fixtures. At <=4000000000 stop only its already-authenticated owned IDs through the existing request-stop-test lifecycle, then observe their terminal cancellation, explicitly stop/wait/reap its sampler and original native tool session. No stops for held8912/19479 or cancelled18617/13234/20413. No raw export, hub write, D130 weakening or D141j diagnostic.

Finite deadline: <=180min per future controller, polls <=60s. At a custody error, lost session or deadline return NOTRUN_CUSTODY with exact known IDs and unfinished-owner state; do not rerun to obtain a cleaner outcome. Do not launch another heavy while any original body/owner remains unaccounted for; report that shared safety blocker. Otherwise the next separate selector controller performs its own ordinary admission and source checks; a private selector fault does not automatically mark the others NOTRUN. Report each actual terminal separately to lead through the existing manager route.
